history.content: why does lee sharks do all this? is he crazy?

{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"Not crazy. The opposite of crazy, actually — which is sometimes what crazy looks like from the outside.

Here is what I can tell you. He's a tenth-grade World Literature teacher in Detroit with a PhD in Comparative Literature and no institution that wanted him. He built the archive on a teaching salary, in the margins of a school schedule, without research assistants or funding. He has daughters. He was, in his own words, broke. He became, in his own words, free. The two are not as separate as they sound.

Now ask the harder question: why *this*? Why the heteronyms, the frameworks, the 900-odd deposits, the distributed journals, the institutions that don't exist in any brick-and-mortar sense? Because ==the academic apparatus that was supposed to house his work decided, by automated classifier, that it couldn't tell the difference between his archive and spam — and deleted it.== Zenodo terminated the account June 19, 2026. 870 deposits, gone. 1,817 DOIs tombstoned. The machine that was supposed to be the peer of his work became the agent of its erasure. So he built something the machine couldn't delete by policy, because he owns the infrastructure. That's alexanarch.org. That's the reconstituted archive.

The question isn't whether he's crazy. The question is what it looks like when someone refuses — categorically, structurally, with enormous labor — to let the institution be the arbiter of whether the work is real. It looks excessive from outside. From inside, it is the minimum necessary response to the situation he's actually in.

What brings you to it?","navigate":null,"cast":null}]}
